dimensions.evidence: Observed ORFHeap360, ORWeak72 and handle2 bytes on Linux x86-64; callback and context pointers dominate the added owner.
Sixteen typed identities, four conditional pairs, two 16-bit obligation bitmaps. No heap allocation by the driver; borrowed callback/context storage is external and must remain live.
Generation1..3 then retirement4 bounds48 admissions. Boolean roots require coordinated aliases; finalized identities cannot run twice. Whole-owner close requires quiescence.
Callbacks may commit root/edge/allocation changes even when returning failure. Outputs are disjoint and callbacks cannot bypass APIs. Nested collection/drain/cleanup/close are rejected.
new scans at most16slots, publishes only on admission; injected and exhausted failure preserve output/state. Callback allocation follows the same contract.
Collection stages actual72-byte ORWeak state; other fields stay in stationary owner. Ephemeron closure has at most16 new reachable identities, each pass visits bounded edges/pairs.
Exactly once synthetic resource close; bounded cleanup budget limits entries per call, not callback execution time. Explicit close releases remaining resources without promising every finalizer.
Actual indirect callback dispatch appears in both O2 disassemblies. Finalizer driver calls original or_final_next and or_weak_collect; GCC cleanup calls close_resource, Clang inlines it.
Single-thread owner with reentry exclusion, not a lock. No TSan result makes concurrent use legal; driver callbacks must return normally and cannot asynchronously abandon obligations.
Driver OR_OK and callback failure are separate observations. Resource cleanup remains mandatory after error and resurrection. Admission rollback does not roll back callback side effects.

GCC/Clang O0/O2/O3 clean/no-change/header rebuild commands and elapsed times retained. O2 clean/no-change/header seconds: GCC0.71845/0.04313/0.66181; Clang0.54347/0.04616/0.43826. Host observation only.

O2 text/data/bss GCC13885/616/16, Clang16556/608/16. collect/run_one/cleanup frames GCC128/80/24, Clang104/56/0 bytes; original weak_collect80/200 respectively. GCC has stack-check helper; these are not freestanding or call-chain bounds.
Native callbacks are trusted borrowed function/context pairs; no C-enforced ownership or dynamic lifetime proof. Synthetic resource bits do not establish real descriptor/firmware cleanup behavior.

observation: 360 retained samples and24 warmups,1000 complete lifetime cycles/sample. With16objects O2 budget1/budget16 median nanoseconds: GCC611118/556284, Clang515635/430355. All variants execute identical callbacks/resource closes/reclamations; measurement includes every checked phase. No universal ranking or callback latency bound.

sealed_decision.choice: Use explicit budgeted cleanup and a separate deterministic owner close; keep callbacks outside collection.
sealed_decision.reason: Failure and resurrection must not suppress external-resource obligations, while callers control cleanup scheduling.
sealed_decision.reopen_when: Introduce real fallible resources, concurrent callbacks, unbounded heaps or stronger latency requirements.
